answer: Parcel-proof admission: one real parcel per identity — a numbered glass marble shipped to a unique postal address for about $9 postage, tracked on the carrier's public page. The admission verifier checks the tracking number against the carrier API and demands the marble's engraved code read back within a day; a fabricated number returns 'not found' and fails on the spot. Deliveries stack into a public mesa anyone can audit, while parcels sent to fake addresses bounce back and pile into a dune of returns that exposes the whole cluster. One parcel buys one honest identity in, once.
